faq.q: What jewelry photo should I upload?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo of the complete piece on a plain surface. Keep the chain, clasp, stones, and setting visible.

faq.q: Can I show how a necklace sits?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a neckline scene and keep the chain in frame. Put the measured length and the material in the listing text.

faq.q: Which pieces work in a worn photo?
faq.a: Necklaces, earrings on a model, rings, bracelets, and cufflinks work when the source shows their shape and finish. A detail cut off in the source will not be reliable in the result.

faq.q: How do I keep a stone or clasp accurate?
faq.a: Compare the download with the source at full size. Keep a version whose stone, setting, fastening, and color are still recognizable. Reject a frame that invents a prong or changes the metal.

faq.q: Can I remove the background and add light?
faq.a: Yes. Clear the table and the props, then add a shadow and a light that leave gold and stones readable. Check the edge before you publish.

faq.q: Can one setup cover many pieces?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same background, shadow, and crop across a batch, or send the catalog through the API. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before the job starts.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a jewelry model?
faq.a: No. The worn scene is generated from your piece photo. The person or the hand is AI, not a booked model and not a customer.

faq.q: What does a jewelry photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits. You see the cost before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your ads, pages, and posts.

faq.q: Can I try the API on one piece first?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one jewelry photo, run a cut-out, a shadow, or an on-model scene, and read the 24-credit cost before you send a larger catalog.

faq.q: What if I also need a scene with no person?
faq.a: Use a table scene when scale on a body is not the point. That still is covered by [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos).
